data.narrative:
Sunfire is a Series E climate and energy company that has raised $315M to date across its funding rounds. The target operates in a sector with a fragmented comparable set: nine peers exist in Climate & Energy broadly, including one public company (Ørsted, LNZA) and eight private firms such as Helion, Redwood Materials, and QuantumScape. However, no cluster of three or more same-stage or adjacent-stage peers with comparable valuation profiles exists, limiting the applicability of peer-median methods.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the only reliable triangulation technique. Using total capital raised ($315M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical of Series E-to-later-stage advancement yields $441M. This single-method result anchors the valuation range, with downside ($375M) and upside ($507M) bounds derived from standard sensitivity adjustments around the median.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $375M to $507M, with a median indication of $441M. Key uncertainties include the absence of a tight peer set for cross-validation and the reliance on stage-progression alone. Any refinement would require either disclosure of comparable transactions in frontier-climate technologies or detailed revenue and margin data to anchor revenue multiple approaches. Until such data materialize, the triangulated range reflects only stage-based progression.
